title: Villes, pays et régions : destination et origine
summary: Learn place names with gender and article, then select `à`, `en`, `au`, `aux` and the corresponding origin phrases.
objectives: Distinguish country gender from a simple final-`e` guess.
Use articles with geographical names and choose location/destination and origin constructions.
Respect established regional and city-name exceptions.

sources.label: OQLF: en, au and dans with American states, consulted 2026-09-07

sections.title: Learn a country or region with its article and grammatical gender
paragraphs: Most country, continent and region names have a conventional article when used as a noun: `la France` (f.), `le Canada` (m.), `les États-Unis` (m. plural), `l'Afrique` (f.), `l'Europe` (f.), `la Bretagne` (f.), `le Québec` (m.), `le Yorkshire` (m.), `la Californie` (f.). The gender is grammatical. A final `-e` often signals a feminine country, but `le Mexique`, `le Cambodge`, `le Mozambique` and `le Zimbabwe` are masculine exceptions.

A vowel does not reveal gender: `l'Iran` is masculine, `l'Italie` feminine, `l'Ontario` masculine. Some place names normally have no article, such as Cuba and Israël. Do not invent an article merely because other country names have one. When a country is the subject or a direct object, its usual article normally stays: `la France est…`, `j'aime le Canada`. A following location preposition can replace or combine with the article.
points: Plural names are plural grammatical phrases, not a separate gender.
Learn both the name and an example location phrase.

examples.note: The country name used as subject keeps its masculine article.

examples.english: I like Brittany and the United States.
examples.note: Region and country names retain their usual articles as direct objects.

examples.french: **Le** Mexique est en Amérique du Nord.

sections.title: Use the same construction for being in and going to a country
paragraphs: For feminine countries and continents, use `en`: `en France`, `en Italie`, `en Afrique`. Masculine countries starting with a vowel also usually take `en`: `en Iran`. Other masculine countries take `au`: `au Canada`, `au Mexique`. Plural countries take `aux`: `aux États-Unis`. The same phrase follows a location verb or a movement verb.

For origin with `venir`, feminine countries/continents and masculine vowel-initial countries normally take `de/d'` without an article: `de France`, `d'Italie`, `d'Afrique`, `d'Iran`. Other masculine countries take `du`; plural countries take `des`. Learn articleless exceptions together with their constructions: `à Cuba/de Cuba`, `en Israël/d'Israël`.

examples.french: Elle habite **en Italie** et vient **de France**.
examples.english: She lives in Italy and comes from France.
examples.note: Feminine country location and origin use `en` and `de/d'`.

examples.french: Nous allons **au Canada**; nous venons **du Mexique**.
examples.english: We are going to Canada; we come from Mexico.

examples.french: Ils vivent **aux États-Unis** et viennent **des États-Unis**.
examples.english: They live in the United States and come from the United States.
examples.note: Plural location and origin use `aux` and `des`.

examples.english: He works in Iran and comes from Iran.
She is going to Cuba, then to Israel.
examples.note: Articleless names still have established individual constructions.

mistakes.why: For ordinary geographical origin, `de France` omits the article; other contexts such as a qualified France can keep it.

sections.title: Cities usually take `à/de`; regions must also be learned by usage
paragraphs: Ordinary city names have no article: `à Montréal/de Montréal`, `à Paris/de Paris`. If an article belongs to the name, retain it and apply contractions where appropriate: `à La Rochelle/de La Rochelle`, `au Havre/du Havre` for `Le Havre`. `À Québec` is Quebec City; `au Québec` is the province.

Many feminine regions take `en`, as in `en Bretagne` and `en Californie`, and Canadian provincial usage includes `au Québec` and `en Ontario`. `Dans` + the usual article is also common for regions, counties and states: `dans le Yorkshire`, `dans les Pays de la Loire`. Gender alone does not predict every region's preferred phrase. American masculine states commonly allow both `au` and `dans le`, such as `au Texas/dans le Texas`; vowel-initial names often allow `en` or `dans l'`, such as `en Arizona/dans l'Arizona`. Do not mark the accepted `dans` forms wrong.

For regional origin use the established `de` phrase: `de Bretagne`, `de Californie`, `d'Ontario`, `du Québec`, `du Yorkshire`, `des Pays de la Loire`. To avoid confusing a state with a city of the same name, use `dans l'État de New York`. These are location constructions, not rules about the political status of a place.
points: Choose the exact place intended: a city and a province can share a name.

examples.french: Je vais **à Québec**, mais je viens **de Montréal**.
examples.english: I am going to Quebec City, but I come from Montreal.
She lives in Quebec and comes from Ontario.

examples.french: Ils travaillent **dans le Yorkshire** et viennent **de Bretagne**.
examples.english: They work in Yorkshire and come from Brittany.
We are going to Le Havre.

examples.french: Il vit **au Texas**, ou, avec une autre tournure, **dans le Texas**.
examples.english: He lives in Texas, or, with another phrasing, in Texas.

sections.title: Establish what the place name identifies before choosing a preposition
paragraphs: A name can refer to a city and to a larger administrative area. `À Genève` identifies the city; `dans le canton de Genève` explicitly identifies the Swiss canton. A construction with `canton`, `province` or `État` is useful when the bare name leaves the reader unsure. It also avoids guessing a regional convention from the city rule.

Look at the whole geographical name rather than its last letter. `Le pays de Galles` (m., Wales) is singular: `pays` ends in `s` even in the singular, and `Galles` does not make the phrase plural. Learn its ordinary location phrase `au pays de Galles` as a unit. This does not change the `aux` pattern for genuinely plural names.
points: `Un canton` (m.) is an administrative canton; `un État` (m.) is a state; `une province` (f.) is a province.

examples.french: Le sentier est **dans le canton de Genève**, loin du centre-ville.
examples.english: The path is in the canton of Geneva, far from the city centre.
examples.note: The named administrative area is explicit.

examples.french: **Le pays de Galles est** à l'ouest de l'Angleterre.
examples.note: The subject is singular despite its spelling.

practice.prompt: Explicitly identify the administrative canton: 'Le chalet est ___ le canton de Vaud.' Supply the preposition.
practice.explanation: Dans le canton de names the area explicitly, rather than treating the canton as a city.

practice.prompt: Complete the city construction, not the canton construction: 'Le congrès a lieu ___ Genève.'
practice.explanation: The ordinary city name takes à.

practice.prompt: Choose au or aux for Wales: 'Ils travaillent ___ pays de Galles.'
practice.explanation: Le pays de Galles is singular; the visible s does not require aux.

practice.prompt: Supply the usual definite article: '___ Canada est grand.'
practice.explanation: Canada is masculine and has an article as subject.

practice.prompt: Supply the usual country preposition: 'Je vais ___ France.'
Supply the origin form: 'Elle vient ___ Canada.'
practice.explanation: Masculine consonant-initial Canada takes du for origin.

practice.prompt: Supply the usual city preposition: 'Il habite ___ Lyon.'
practice.explanation: An ordinary city name takes à.

practice.prompt: Choose le or la for the country: '___ Mexique'.
practice.explanation: Mexique is a masculine exception despite final e.

practice.prompt: Supply the normal article before the continent as direct object: 'J'aime ___ Afrique.'
practice.explanation: Afrique is feminine, but la elides before its vowel.

practice.prompt: Supply the usual location form: 'Elle habite ___ États-Unis.'
practice.explanation: The plural country name takes aux.

practice.prompt: Supply the usual location preposition: 'Nous travaillons ___ Iran.'
practice.explanation: Masculine Iran begins with a vowel, so it takes en.

practice.prompt: Supply the ordinary origin form: 'Il vient ___ Italie.'
practice.explanation: Ordinary origin from feminine Italie uses d' without an article.

practice.prompt: Use dans and the usual article before Yorkshire: 'Nous vivons ___ Yorkshire.'
practice.explanation: This region commonly uses dans le.

practice.prompt: Supply en or dans for the usual articleless regional construction: 'Elle travaille ___ Californie.'
practice.explanation: Feminine Californie uses en in this construction.

practice.prompt: Supply the usual origin preposition: 'Je viens ___ Paris.'
practice.explanation: An ordinary city takes de for origin.

practice.prompt: Supply the origin form: 'Ils viennent ___ États-Unis.'
Use à with the city Le Havre, contracting correctly: 'Je vais ___ Havre.'
practice.explanation: À contracts with the Le belonging to the city name.

practice.prompt: Supply the ordinary origin form for the province: 'Elle vient ___ Québec.'
practice.explanation: Du Québec refers to the province; de Québec would refer to the city.

practice.prompt: Is 'dans le Texas' an accepted alternative to 'au Texas'?
practice.explanation: OQLF accepts both constructions; do not turn a preference into a prohibition.

production_task.prompt: Introduce two people's origins and current homes. Include one city, one feminine country and one masculine country; give the city/province distinction clearly if using Québec.
production_task.model_answer: Je viens de France et j'habite à Montréal. Mon ami vient du Canada et travaille en Italie.
production_task.translation: I come from France and live in Montreal. My friend comes from Canada and works in Italy.
rubric: Use `de/d'`, `du` or `des` for origin as appropriate.
Use `à` for the ordinary city name.
Choose `en/au/aux` from the country construction, not a direct English translation.
